verdict.rationale: Phaser has the ingredients for good LLM output: a widely used npm package (4.2.1, ~263k weekly downloads), full TypeScript definitions that editors pick up automatically, concept docs with code patterns, and a live llms.txt examples index with an examples API. Community users also praise how easy and straightforward it is. API stability is undermined, though: the docs admit Phaser 2 code and tutorials 'likely won't work in Phaser 3', the current major is 4.x, and multiple community threads call the docs outdated or poor, so models trained on mixed-version examples are likely to produce stale code. Missing for 10: evidence of API stability across major versions, any hands-on evidence that LLM-generated Phaser code works first try, consistently well-regarded documentation, and docs.phaser.io llms.txt/markdown endpoints (both return 404).
